::: {#thm-complement-dfa}
#### Swapping the accepting states

Let $M = (S, \Sigma, \delta, s_0, F)$ be a DFA (@def-dfa), and let

$$
M' = (S, \Sigma, \delta, s_0, S \setminus F)
$$

be the DFA with the same states, inputs, transitions and initial state, whose accepting states are the states that are not accepting in $M$.
Then $L(M')$ (@def-automaton-language) is the complement (@def-complement) $\Sigma^* \setminus L(M)$ of $L(M)$ in $\Sigma^*$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

The extended transition function $\delta^*$ (@def-extended-transition) is built from $S$, $\Sigma$ and $\delta$ alone,
so $M$ and $M'$ have the same $\delta^*$.
Let $w \in \Sigma^*$.
By the language of a DFA (@def-automaton-language) and the definition of accepting (@def-accept),

$$
\ba
w \in L(M')
&\iff M' \text{ accepts } w
&& \text{(language of a DFA)}
\\&\iff \delta^*(s_0, w) \in S \setminus F
&& \text{(definition of accepting)}
\\&\iff \delta^*(s_0, w) \notin F
&& \text{(since } \delta^*(s_0, w) \in S \text{)}
\\&\iff M \text{ does not accept } w
&& \text{(definition of accepting)}
\\&\iff w \notin L(M).
&& \text{(language of a DFA)}
\ea
$$

So $L(M')$ is the set of strings in $\Sigma^*$ that are not in $L(M)$.

The step from $\delta^*(s_0, w) \in S \setminus F$ to $\delta^*(s_0, w) \notin F$ uses that $\delta$ is a function on all of $S \times \Sigma$,
so that $\delta^*(s_0, w)$ is a state of $S$ for every string $w$.
Some drawings of automata leave out a dead state (@def-dead-state) and the arrows into it, so that some states have no arrow for some input.
Swapping the accepting states of such a drawing does not give the complement:
a string whose run would enter the missing dead state is rejected before and after the swap.
Put the dead state back before swapping.

:::

:::
